title: Calling ‘cross’ a mere metonymy for Christ breaks where the hymn opposes and distinguishes the cross from Christ
source_text: XXIV. Vim autem manifestam verbis ipsis faciunt, qui, ut absurdum istud vitent, hodie volunt crucem, per Metonymiam quandam, pro Christo ipso accipi in ejusmodi precationibus. Nam quae loquendi leges patiuntur, ut crux pro Christo crucifixo sumatur, iis ipsis in locis ubi Christo opponitur, & a Christo contradistinguitur, & celebratur tanquam contactu corporis Christi nobilitata?
pass_a_gloss: But they do open violence to the words themselves who, to avoid that absurdity, today will have the cross taken by a certain Metonymy for Christ Himself in prayers of that kind. For what laws of speaking allow the cross to be taken for the crucified Christ in those very places where it is opposed to Christ, and is contradistinguished from Christ, and is celebrated as ennobled by contact with Christ’s body?
pass_b_english: Modern metonymy (‘cross’ = Christ) cannot rescue texts that oppose, distinguish, and praise the cross by bodily contact apart from Christ.

choices.english: open violence to the words themselves
choices.why: Blocks the soft reading of cross-prayers.
rejected: no real address to the cross
